forms: name the place of a digit
which digit is in a named place
how many places a number has
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child names the place of any digit (ones to hundred millions), including digits beside zeros, and says which digit sits in a named place. Numbers come from real settings such as a county budget or the number of phone lines.

forms: total value of an underlined digit
total values of two digits added
difference between two digits of the same value
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.TOTAL_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child gives the total value of a chosen digit (digit times its place), adds the total values of two digits, and writes the number in expanded form. The child does not mistake a digit for its total value.

forms: read a number aloud in groups
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SYMBOLS_HM.mastery: Given a number said or written in parts (for example 45 million, 12 thousand and 7) the child writes it in figures with every place filled and zero as a place holder, and reads a figure aloud in groups of three. Numbers up to 999,999,999.

forms: choose the words for a figure
write a cheque amount in words
spot the mistake in the words
say the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_FROM_.mastery: The child writes a number up to 9,999,999 in words with British spelling, a hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine, and each group (millions, thousands, hundreds) in order. Zeros in a group are not spoken. The design limit for words is millions.

forms: order two numbers given in words
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.FIGURES_FRO.mastery: Given a number in words up to millions, such as "two million and forty-five thousand and seven", the child writes it in figures with zero place holders in every empty place.

forms: round the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_TO_PL.mastery: The child rounds a number up to 999,999,999 to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, million, ten million or hundred million: looks at the digit just to the right, rounds up on 5 or more, and writes zeros in all places after the one rounded.

forms: round the number in a report
why a rounded number is not exact
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_IN_CO.mastery: Given a real setting (a population, a county budget, a news report) the child chooses the sensible place to round to, rounds the number, and says why the rounded number is only an estimate. Rounding a carried digit (such as 999,500 to the nearest thousand) is included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.EVEN_ODD.mastery: The child classifies any whole number up to millions as even or odd by its last digit, and knows that sums and products of even and odd numbers follow a pattern (even + even is even, odd + odd is even, even x anything is even).

forms: pick the primes from a table
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PRIME_NUMBE.mastery: The child tells prime from composite numbers up to 100 by testing small divisors, knows that 1 is neither, that 2 is the only even prime, and that an odd number is not always prime. The child lists the primes up to 50.

forms: sum or difference in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ADD_SUB_LAR.mastery: The child adds and subtracts whole numbers of up to nine digits in a column, regrouping across zeros, and decides whether to add or subtract in a story about money, population or distance. Answers are checked by estimating.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.MULT_LARGE.mastery: The child multiplies a number of up to 4 digits by a number of up to 3 digits using long multiplication, with the zero place holder in the second and third rows, and by 10, 100 and 1,000 by shifting the digits. The product is checked by estimating.

forms: what the remainder means in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.DIV_LARGE.mastery: The child divides a number of up to 6 digits by a number of up to 3 digits by long division, with zeros in the quotient where a digit does not fit, writes the remainder as a whole number, and checks by multiplying back.

forms: put in brackets to make a value
find the mistake in the order
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ORDER_OF_OP.mastery: The child works out expressions of up to three operations with brackets, working brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Numbers up to 3 digits.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.OPERATIONS_.mastery: The child reads a story with two or three steps (fares, fuel, rent, bags and rows), chooses the operations, works them in order and writes the answer with its unit. Money left, total takings and equal sharing are included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_EXTEND_.mastery: Given the first four to six terms of a sequence with a constant difference or a constant multiplier, the child finds the rule, continues the sequence, and spots a term that does not fit.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_NTH_TER.mastery: For a sequence that goes up or down by the same amount, the child finds a distant term (for example the 12th) by first term plus the number of steps times the difference, and does not count the first term as a step.

forms: write the terms from a rule
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_CREATE_.mastery: Given a rule such as "start at 5, add 4" or "multiply by 3 then add 3", the child writes the first terms, and makes a sequence of their own for a number game, checking that the terms follow the rule every time.
